messages:
lucy: quick flag 1: our onboarding smoke for sample-apps flagged a weird runtime error on Cloudflare Pages edge after upgrading @redwood/sdk to a patch that changed exports map. looks like an ESM default import mismatch.

lucy: stack: `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor` in edge/handler.mjs at import boundary. Node serverless and local node tests OK.

nikhil: hmm. did we remove the explicit .mjs entry? iirc the patch collapsed exports to a single path to reduce duplication. that can break environments that require explicit import vs require conditions.

emily: saw reports from a user who uses esbuild + externalize. bundlers that rewrite imports may end up resolving the CJS file for ESM consumers if exports isn't conditional.

joel: quick check of package.json in the release branch shows: "exports": { ".": "./lib/index.js" } and "main" pointing to lib/index.cjs. so there's a mismatch. Node 14+ resolver may pick the .js as ESM in some bundlers, but the file is actually CJS built as .js which causes default import problems.

lucy: ugh. so the file extension alone isn't a reliable indicator. we should use conditional exports with explicit "import" and "require" targets AND make our ESM build use .mjs or properly set "type": "module" in that subpath.

nikhil: also the types entry was switched to point to dist/index.d.ts which is a generated declaration using `export =` style. TS consumers that do `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'` see incompatible shape. i think our dts generator picked the wrong moduleKind.

emily: workaround: in sample-apps we pinned to @redwood/sdk@1.3.x for the CI edge runs and added a quick import-only smoke test: `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk'
console.log(typeof SDK)` to fail fast on import anomalies.

joel: recommendation: revert to an explicit export map: { ".": { "import": "./esm/index.mjs", "require": "./cjs/index.cjs" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" } plus update "types" to point to esm/index.d.ts if we publish ESM typings. This keeps bundlers and edge runtimes deterministic.

lucy: agreed. can we do a patch release 1.4.2 that reintroduces conditional mapping and fixes types? customers onboarding this week.

nikhil: i'll prepare the patch, and add a small test in the SDK repo test-suite: run node --input-type=module to import esm build and run `node -e "import('@redwood/sdk').then(m=>console.log('ok'))"`. Also add an esbuild + cloudflare pages smoke matrix in CI.

emily: also worth adding a short DX note in the README about "default export vs named" and recommend `esModuleInterop` or using `import * as Redwood` as a safe pattern until we stabilize typings.

joel: FYI bundlers: rollup and esbuild treat .js extension differently when package.json has "type": "module" or conditional exports. We need to be explicit rather than rely on heuristics.

ci-bot: ci: start job edge-smoke-matrix (job 442)

nikhil: publishing 1.4.2-prerelease with fixes to exports/types now. linking when ready.

lucy: thx. once published i'll run sample-apps matrix and follow up in the onboarding doc.

nikhil: published 1.4.2-canary: https://npmjs.com/package/@redwood/sdk/v/1.4.2-canary. smoke passed locally in CF Pages emulator.

lucy: sample-apps edge matrix: all green on canary. planning to ship stable patch tomorrow morning.

emily: opened a small DX page: "Package exports & edge runtimes" in docs repo with examples for node, bundlers, and edge. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/78

joel: follow-ups:
- add export map permutations unit tests (sdk infra)
- add edge import smoke to sample-apps CI (done)
- include types sanity check in publish pipeline (nikhil)

lucy: great catch everyone. export map churn is low-severity but high-friction for new users. we should include this in our release playbook checklist.
